clue.text: P for Pinter, broadcasting John's gas with Robin

parts.note: John Birt was Director-General of the BBC in the 1990s, the broadcasting boss
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen, a gas
Sir Robin Day was a famous BBC political interviewer, another broadcaster

explanation.surface: A Pinter-themed broadcast pairs one BBC grandee's hot air with another's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcasting' does double service in the surface, setting both Johns and Robins in the BBC; P stands for PARTY throughout the puzzle, so The Birthday Party is Pinter's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Pinter wrote the play The Birthday Party, so this word goes before the puzzle's P to name his work.

clue.text: Traveller to support 1977's cricketing circus?

parts.note: to back is to support
Kerry Packer set up World Series Cricket in 1977, nicknamed Packer's circus

explanation.surface: A traveller supports the breakaway cricket series of the late 1970s.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1977 the Australian media owner Kerry Packer signed top cricketers for his rival World Series, dubbed a circus.
explanation.definitionFit: A backpacker is a budget traveller who carries belongings in a rucksack.

clue.text: King of Italy's TV provider absorbs everything that one can remember

parts.note: re is Italian for king

indicators.note: absorbs means the word for TV provider takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: cable is a television service
all means everything

explanation.surface: An Italian monarch's television company takes in everything memorable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King of Italy' points to a person, but it is the Italian word for king, a crossword favourite; 'absorbs' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recallable can be called back to mind, which is what one can remember.

clue.text: Very masculine sheep in a tizzy

parts.note: a he-man is very masculine, so he works as a word for male
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A ram that is all male is in a flap.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worked up or agitated is what being in a tizzy means, an idiom for flustered.

clue.text: Nursing officer is, I can reveal, outside, being employed by Nick Park

indicators.note: outside means the shuffled letters go round the next piece
reveal hints that the letters are opened up and shown in a new order

parts.note: a matron is a senior nurse in charge of a ward

explanation.surface: A hospital matron confides something about working for the famous animator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reveal' shuffles IS I CAN to ANI ICS, which goes 'outside' MATRON. Nick Park made Wallace and Gromit; strictly that is clay animation.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Park's studio works in animation of models, loosely called animatronics, the use of moving puppets in film.

clue.text: Place of religion is to get a fellow elevated

parts.note: a chap is a fellow, a man
EL is the American elevated railway, as in Chicago's El

explanation.surface: A church is where a man can feel lifted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' looks like a description of the fellow's mood, but it is the US EL, short for elevated railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small building or room set aside for Christian worship.

clue.text: Publicity for model in middle available if you're quick off the mark

definitions.text: available if you're quick off the mark

indicators.note: in means the first pieces sit inside the word for middle

parts.note: the heart is the middle of something
ads are publicity
Henry Ford's Model T car

explanation.surface: Advertising for a fashion model stuck in the centre of attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' points to a fashion model, but it is the T of Ford's Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is an early advantage, the kind you gain by being quick to begin.

clue.text: Spoil the P at the stern?

definitions.meaning: with P standing for party, a party pooper spoils it
the raised deck at the stern of a ship

explanation.definitionFit: Poop means spoil, as in party pooper, and a ship's poop deck is at the stern.

clue.text: Fun bird?

definitions.meaning: a bit of fun or a prank

explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a frolic, and also a songbird such as the skylark.

clue.text: P for Eliot: prepare to shoot follower

parts.note: to cock a gun is to raise the hammer ready for firing
a tail is someone who follows a suspect

explanation.surface: An Eliot-themed scene where a gunman readies his weapon against the man tailing him.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for PARTY throughout; T S Eliot wrote the verse play The Cocktail Party.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot's verse drama is The Cocktail Party, so this word goes before the puzzle's P to name it.

clue.text: P before 1 across

definitions.meaning: with P standing for party, the ... Party is the British left-of-centre political party
..., the work of giving birth, comes just before a child's first birth date

explanation.walkthrough: P means PARTY throughout; 1 across is BIRTHDAY, and a mother's labour comes right before the day of birth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour Party is a major British party, and labour in childbirth precedes the day of a baby's arrival.

clue.text: P at 4 in a jam

indicators.note: in tells us that one group of letters is placed inside the word for jam

parts.note: conserve is jam, fruit preserved with sugar
taken as written
IV is 4 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A party stuck at four o'clock in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a jam' reads as an idiom for trouble, but 'in' is the container signal and jam is the outer word. P means PARTY throughout, the Conservatives being the British Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: The Conservative Party is one of Britain's two main political parties, so the word completes the puzzle's P.

clue.text: Potentially happy soul about to become open-mouthed

indicators.note: about here means surrounding: the shuffled letters go round the next piece
something that is potentially another thing could be rearranged into it, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: go can mean become, as in go green or go mad

explanation.surface: A cheerful person might be about to start gaping in astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potentially' shuffles HAPPY SOUL into POLYPHAUS, and 'about' puts GO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyphagous animal eats many kinds of food, so it is figuratively open-mouthed to anything edible.

clue.text: I'm devoted to reptiles: work (hard) I get round to in due course

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
H stands for hard, as on pencils
O is round in shape
later means in due course

explanation.surface: A snake lover says they'll get round to hard work eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: An ophiolater is a snake-worshipper, one devoted to serpents.

clue.text: Begging to repair vessel in the cold

parts.note: to mend is to repair

indicators.note: in places the vessel inside the word for cold

parts.note: icy means cold
a can is a container

explanation.surface: Asking for alms to fix a container out in the freezing cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendicancy is the state or practice of living by begging.

clue.text: P travelling — train?

definitions.meaning: with P standing for party, a ... party is a group travelling together by bus

explanation.definitionFit: A coach party is a travelling group, and coaching someone means training them in a skill.

clue.text: Be aware of a calf keeping its head in the shade

indicators.note: in places the calf pieces inside the word for shade

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour

indicators.note: keeping means the word for calf holds the next letter

parts.note: veal is calf meat
the calf's head is its first letter, C

explanation.surface: Know about a young cow that keeps its head while standing in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its head' is the calf's own first letter, held by 'keeping'; the whole calf group then sits 'in' the shade. Veal for a live calf is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a clue is to know something, an idiom for being aware of it.

clue.text: Clove got up by pupil

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, to get up
the apple of the eye is an old name for the pupil

explanation.surface: A spice is raised by a schoolchild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' suggests a schoolchild, but the apple of the eye is the pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose apple belongs to the same plant genus, Syzygium, as the clove tree, so clove serves loosely as a genus name.

clue.text: Animator goes offline for a lot of worship

indicators.note: goes, read with the off of offline as goes off, says the letters go haywire

parts.note: the word line, which the off joins with goes to be shuffled

indicators.note: a lot of but not all of the word, so its final letters are dropped

parts.note: to venerate is to worship

explanation.surface: Someone who livens things up goes offline for long stretches of prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes off' scrambles LINE into ENLI; 'a lot of' trims VENERATE to VENER by dropping ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An animator is one who gives life or spirit to something, just as an enlivener does.

clue.text: Placed P for someone else

definitions.meaning: placed in a race means finishing in the top three
with P standing for party, a ... party is an outsider to an agreement

explanation.definitionFit: Being placed in a race can mean coming third, and a third party is someone outside the main two.

clue.text: Michael's maybe going to help bar change licensee

indicators.note: going to help suggests the clue words each lend part of themselves to make the answer

explanation.surface: A pub's change of landlord is going to help a man named Michael.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across bAR CHANGE LICensee; the indicator is loose, the words 'going to help' to form the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael is an archangel, so a quality of his, maybe, is archangelic.

clue.text: Riding on horse, increase your speed

indicators.note: on means one piece sits on top of the other in the down entry

parts.note: gee or gee-gee is a child's word for horse
up means riding, as a jockey is up on a horse

explanation.surface: A rider urges the horse to go faster.
explanation.walkthrough: Gee up is also what riders call to a horse, so the surface and answer meet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee up means hurry up or go faster, a call to urge on a horse.

clue.text: Not up first at bottom of sea

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the word at

parts.note: the seabed is the bottom of the sea

explanation.surface: First lying on the ocean floor, not yet risen.
explanation.definitionFit: Abed means in bed, so not up yet.

clue.text: P for self-starter on day in Berlin

indicators.note: starter means the opening letter of self

parts.note: Tag is German for day

explanation.surface: A party for a self-starter held on a day in Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for PARTY throughout; a stag party is a groom's night out.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party is a bachelor party, so this word completes the puzzle's P.

clue.text: P requires courage

definitions.meaning: with P standing for party, a ... party is one where each guest brings drink
... is British slang for nerve, as in to lose your ...

explanation.definitionFit: A bottle party has guests bring wine, and bottle is British slang for nerve or courage.

clue.text: It turns green once church leaves Devon town

indicators.note: turns tells us the word It is read backwards

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry

indicators.note: leaves means the letters for church depart from the word once

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Something changes colour after the church leaves a town in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It turns' gives TI; 'once church leaves' takes CE out of ONCE to leave ON. Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiverton is a market town in mid-Devon, in south-west England.

clue.text: Followed with resolution

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means trailed or followed closely
... as an adjective means stubbornly determined

explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them, and a dogged person acts with tenacious resolve.

clue.text: Food and drink at P separated but turned around

indicators.note: around tells us the reversed word goes round the word for separated
turned tells us the word for but is read backwards

parts.note: yet can mean but, as in strange yet true
apart means separated

explanation.surface: Refreshments at a gathering where people split up but then came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives TEY; 'around' wraps it round the word for separated. P means PARTY throughout, so the definition is refreshment at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea party is a gathering where tea, with food and drink, is served, matching refreshment at a gathering.
